title: VP/Director of Health Safety, Environmental & Regulatory (HSE&R)
description: TITLE: Vice President / Director of Health Safety, Environmental & Regulatory (HSE&R) Please note: Title and compensation will be assigned commensurate with the candidate’s experience. ABOUT THE COMPANY: W&T Offshore, Inc. (NYSE: WTI) is a thriving, independent oil and natural gas producer operating in the Gulf of America, the second-largest producing basin in the U.S. for nearly four decades. ABOUT OUR EMPLOYEES: We have built a team of talented and collaborative individuals who are committed to cultivating a culture of integrity, honesty, trust, respect, and communication. Our mission is to attract and retain like-minded team members who will grow and prosper within our W&T community. W&T offers a competitive total rewards program designed to provide competitive pay, health and financial benefits, and work-life balance. WORKING LOCATION: Houston Office - 5718 WESTHEIMER RD 7 7057 FULL-TIME/PART-TIME: Full-Time SCHEDULE: Mon -Thurs - 9 hours /Friday - 4 hours (in-office) FLSA STATUS: Salary, Non-Exempt POSITION SUMMARY: Reporting to the COO, The Vice President / Director of Health, Safety, Environment & Regulatory (HSE&R) assumes responsibility for guiding the formulation, execution, administration, and continuous enhancement of the Company's safety and environmental strategies and objectives. This role calls for the delivery of expert guidance in health, safety, environmental and regulatory matters to lead and bolster all levels of the organization’s operations. The VP, HSE&R is hands-on and requires current EHS leadership experience (policies and procedures, processes, system implementations, ESG reporting, compliance, regulatory) specific to the regulatory requirements of the offshore oil and gas industry and a publicly traded company. The role is office-based Mon-Thurs (remote Friday) with up to 15% travel to within the company’s operating area (TX, LA, AL). Primary Responsibilities Manage HSE&R Department, with staff located in Houston (TX), New Iberia (LA), Mobile (AL) and Gulf of America (Offshore). Provide HSE&R leadership to all departments including drilling, completions, operations, production, P&A and construction activities, through leading by example and working constructively with the other department managers and staff. Manage W&T’s regulatory responsibilities for all operations, including preparation and submittal of EPs, DOCDs, permit applications and other filings with BSEE, BOEM and applicable State regulators. Responsible for ESG data collection and reporting. Revise and develop key corporate H&S and environmental policies, programs and procedures and roll them out to all business units and departments through face-to-face and online training. Work with in-house and external attorneys on regulatory enforcement and other legal matters. Represent W&T in Industry groups such as the Offshore Operators Committee and API, and with consortiums such as Clean Gulf Associates and Helix Well Control Group. Manage the company’s HSE compliance programs, including performance tracking and reporting both internally and to regulatory agencies. Track all HSE metrics on a routine basis; develop presentation material for executive management’s use. Direct company HSE/SEMS audits, both internally and externally using contractors and internal compliance technicians. Direct effective incident investigations and review and approve final investigation reports and disseminate the lessons learned. Lead efforts for emergency response training and drills. Continue to implement the computer-based Environmental Management Systems for SEMS and compliance. Manage W&T’s drug testing program. Manage the company’s contractor management program, with ISNetworld and internal processes. Manage and direct W&T’s SEMS program for continuous improvement. Manage waste disposal activities to ensure compliance with RCRA, Alabama, Louisiana and Texas waste regulations. Manage all air permitting activities onshore, including the proper installation of pollution control devices and emissions testing and reporting. Also manage all Greenhouse Gas reporting for offshore and onshore. Knowledge, Education & Experience Bachelor of Science degree in Environmental Management, Science, Engineering or equivalent. 15+ years of hands-on Senior HSE management experience and demonstrated track record managing significant HSE programs in the offshore energy sector. Exceptional leadership, organizational and problem-solving skills. Demonstrated quality decision making skills. Highly effective communication and interpersonal skills with the ability to establish excellent working relationships at both the field and management level. Excellent written and oral communication skills. Proven experience communicating and negotiating with government agencies such as BSEE (MMA), BOEM, USCG and State regulators. Knowledge of applicable regulations that are implemented and enforced by BSEE (MMA), BOEM, USCG, OSHA, EPA, PHMSA, AOGB, APSC, ADEM, TRRC and TGLO. Proven experience managing effective SEMS programs. Strong time management, prioritization, and organizational skills Proficiency with all MS Office products (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, etc.) Self-motivated with the ability to adapt work schedule as needed to accomplish objectives. Knowledge of SempCheck or similar computer-based EMS systems Safety or environmental certification, such as CSP is a plus. Physical Requirements Ability to travel offshore as needed via helicopter and/or boat. Ability to pass all required safety training for offshore travel/work. Requires prolonged sitting, some bending and stooping. Occasional lifting up to 10 pounds. Manual dexterity sufficient to operate a computer keyboard and calculator. This description is intended to describe the type of work being performed by a person assigned to this position. title: Facility Security Officer
description: Join the company that’s building the telemetry infrastructure for the AI era. At Cribl , we partner with IT and Security teams at many of the world’s biggest enterprises, including half of the Fortune 100, to bridge the gap between AI ambition and infrastructure reality. As the AI Platform for Telemetry, we give customers the choice, control, and flexibility to manage and analyze telemetry for both humans and agents, so they can build what’s next. We’re one of the fastest‑growing private companies and a leading player in a massive, fast‑moving market. With a global workforce, we’re remote‑first and grounded in a simple idea: software is a people business. Cribl is the place where curious, collaborative people can do their best work, grow fast, and bring their full selves to the herd. Why You’ll Love This Role Cribl is hiring a Facility Security Officer to build and manage our industrial security program as our federal business grows. You will serve as Cribl’s appointed FSO of record with the Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency (DCSA), own the Facility Clearance (FCL) program, and support compliance with the National Industrial Security Program and 32 CFR Part 117. This is an industrial-security role—not a guard or general office-security position. You will partner with Legal, People Operations, Contracts, Public Sector Sales, IT, Workplace, and Security & Compliance. We’re looking for a Sr Security & Compliance Engineer to join our team! As An Active Member Of Our Team, You Will… Manage FCL sponsorship and maintenance in NISS, including SF-328, KMP designations, changed conditions, and FOCI reporting. Manage the cleared-personnel lifecycle in DISS/NBIS, including sponsorship, investigations, reinvestigations, continuous vetting, transfers, debriefings, and terminations. Guide applicants through eApp and maintain accurate, confidential personnel-security records. Deliver initial, annual, insider-threat, foreign-travel, and other required security briefings. Review and maintain DD Form 254s, process visit authorizations, and advise Contracts and Legal on security requirements before commitments are made. Conduct annual self-inspections, prepare required certifications and reports, maintain corrective actions, and lead preparation for DCSA Security Reviews. Serve as Cribl’s primary point of contact with DCSA and the trusted advisor to executives and cross-functional teams on government security requirements. Partner with Workplace and Facilities on access control, visitor management, secure-area requirements, and other facility controls applicable to cleared work. Establish and maintain security policies, procedures, records, and training programs. We are a remote-first company and work happens across many time-zones - you may be required to occasionally perform duties outside your standard working hours. If You’ve Got It - We Want It U.S. citizenship and an active U.S. Government Secret clearance, with the ability to obtain and maintain Top Secret. 7+ years of industrial- or personnel-security experience, including 3+ years as an appointed FSO or Assistant FSO at a cleared contractor. Working knowledge of 32 CFR Part 117 and the NISPOM. Hands-on experience with DISS/NBIS, NISS, eApp, FCL processing, SF-328/FOCI, DD Form 254s, self-inspections, and DCSA Security Reviews. Completion of the applicable DCSA/CDSE FSO curriculum through STEPP, or the ability to complete it within six months of appointment. Experience standing up a security program or taking a facility through an initial FCL. Strong writing, communication, organization, discretion, and judgment. Ability to work effectively across a distributed, remote-first organization. Preferred Skills Experience in a commercial software, SaaS, cloud, or technology company. SPēD or NCMS ISP® certification. Familiarity with ITPSO responsibilities, FedRAMP, CMMC, DFARS, or CUI requirements. Familiarity with Cribl products or observability technologies. #LI-KJ1 #LI-Remote The salary for this role is dependent on geographic location and will be based on the individual candidate's job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. In addition to base salary, for sales and some sales-adjacent roles, employees are eligible to earn incentive compensation (commission). For all other roles, employees are eligible to participate in the Cribl Corporate Bonus Program. In addition to a competitive salary, Cribl also offers a generous benefits package which includes health, dental, vision, short-term disability, and life insurance, paid holidays and paid time off, a fertility treatment benefit, 401(k), and equity. title: VP Health, Safety & Environmental
description: Job Family Group HSSE Group Job Description About us Our purpose is to bring together people, energy and markets to power and navigate a changing world. In a time of constant change and possibility we need new talent to pursue commercial opportunities, fueled by world-class insight and expertise. We’re always striving for more innovative digital solutions, sustainable outcomes and closer collaboration across our company and beyond, and you could be part of that too. Together we continue to grow as the world’s leading energy company! Role Purpose As the Vice President, Health, Safety & Environmental (HS&E) you are responsible for setting the strategic direction and providing executive leadership for HSSE performance across bp's U.S. Convenience & Mobility business. This role serves as the senior HS&E leader for a large, geographically dispersed operation encompassing company-owned retail sites, franchise locations, bakery operations, field teams, offices, and support functions across the United States. The Vice President is accountable for developing and delivering an integrated HS&E strategy that protects people, communities, assets, brand reputation, and business performance while enabling sustainable growth. The role ensures compliance with all regulatory requirements and bp standards while fostering a culture where safety, risk management, operational rigor, and environmental stewardship are embedded into every aspect of the business. Partnering closely with executive leadership, operations teams, franchise partners, and bp's central HS&E organization, the Vice President will establish enterprise-wide standards, strengthen risk management capabilities, drive continuous improvement, and ensure consistent execution of HS&E programs across a network supporting thousands of employees, contractors, customers, and business partners. This leader will provide oversight for operational risk management, process safety, occupational safety, environmental compliance, emergency preparedness and response, incident prevention, regulatory engagement, and business resilience. The role plays a critical part in enabling safe and reliable operations while supporting commercial performance, transformation initiatives, network growth, and long-term value creation. The Vice President will serve as a trusted advisor to bp’s US Convenience & Mobility leadership team, ensuring HS&E risks are identified, understood, and managed effectively while driving a culture of accountability, learning, and continuous improvement throughout the organization. Key Accountabilities Own the USCM Health, Safety & Environmental strategy and operating plan, ensuring risks across sites, fueling operations and store environments are identified, managed and mitigated. Serve as the senior advisor to the USCM leadership on health, safety, environmental, security, and operational risk matters. Lead the USCM HSSE team, setting clear priorities, performance expectations and accountability for safety and environmental outcomes across the network. Maintain a strong dotted-line relationship with bp's central HSSE function to ensure USCM continues to apply enterprise standards, tools and governance expectations. Ensure compliance with all applicable federal, state and local health, safety and environmental regulations, including DOT, OSHA and EPA requirements, across USCM's store and fueling network. Partner with Operations, Construction & Maintenance and Store Support teams to embed safety and environmental considerations into site design, store operations and field execution. Lead incident investigation, root cause analysis and corrective action processes, translating lessons learned into practical improvements at store level. Provide regular reporting on safety performance, environmental compliance and emerging risks to the USCM CEO and leadership team. Skills & Experience Significant experience in health, safety, environmental or risk management leadership, ideally within convenience retail, fuel retail, grocery or another multi-site operating environment. Strong understanding of HSSE regulatory requirements applicable to retail fueling and convenience store operations, including DOT, OSHA and EPA standards. Experience leading HSSE teams and building a hands-on, field-credible safety culture across a distributed, multi-site network. Proven ability to work across matrixed reporting lines while maintaining clear accountability and independence of judgement. Strong incident investigation, risk assessment and corrective action experience. Bachelor's degree in occupational safety, environmental science, or a related field preferred; equivalent experience will be considered. Who You Will Work With You'll work with bp's central HSSE function, Operations, Construction & Maintenance, Store Support Organizations, and Legal/Compliance. This role reports to the USCM CEO, with a dotted line into bp's central HSSE function. Why join BP At BP, we support our people to learn and grow in a diverse and challenging environment. We believe that our team is strengthened by diversity. We are committed to fostering an inclusive environment in which everyone is respected and treated fairly. There are many aspects of our employees’ lives that are meaningful, so we offer benefits to enable your work to fit with your life. These benefits can include flexible working options, a generous paid parental leave policy, and excellent retirement benefits, among others. Travel Requirement Up to 50% travel should be expected with this role Relocation Assistance: Relocation may be negotiable for this role Remote Type This position is a hybrid of office/remote working Skills Accounting for people, Accounting for people, Agility core practices, Communication, Continuous Learning, Cost-conscious decision-making, Cost Leadership, Cost Performance Management, Crisis and emergency response management, Decision Making, Driving and transport safety, Fire incident response, Hazard Id

title: Vice President, Global Environmental, Health, and Safety
description: TPI Composites, a trusted, long-term manufacturing partner to the global wind energy market, provides high-quality, cost-effective composite wind blades backed by advanced manufacturing capabilities and our proprietary, AI driven BladeAssure™ validation platform. TPI is headquartered in Scottsdale, Arizona, operates factories in the U.S. and Mexico and has an engineering development center in Denmark with global service operations in the U.S., Mexico, and EU. Job Description Reporting to the Chief Operating Officer, the Vice President, Environmental Health, Safety and Sustainability provides strategic direction and leadership for TPI’s environmental, health & safety programs. The incumbent is responsible for the continuous development and effective implementation of Safety Policies and Procedures. In addition, the incumbent leads the company’s sustainability program. He/she leads a team of safety professionals to drive and ensure a proactive safety culture across the organization as well as best in class sustainability practices. Key stakeholders include regional business leaders, customers as well as the Senior Leadership team at TPI Responsibilities & Accountabilities Drive a proactive safety culture across the organization Design, implement, and continuously improve enterprise-wide environmental, health & safety strategy and programs consistent with industry best practices, Define short and long term objectives to achieve company safety and sustainability goals and implement KPI’s, monthly reporting and business reviews to communicate progress Assess and drive implementation of optimal health & safety organizational structure, tools, training, programs, governance, and accountability models Leads efforts of safety organization through matrix leadership Provide technical expertise and thought leadership, create synergies and leverage knowledge, personnel, best practices, and resources across the organization Support the company’s US Worker’s Compensation Program effectively. This includes a focus on effective case management, return-to-work programs, and similar relative to work related illness and injuries. Ensure compliance with all environmental, health, and safety standards Monitor and facilitate the progress of environmental sustainability programs and governance systems, consistent with strategies, goals, measurements and reporting standards Lead the organization to behave with a sense of urgency, ensure that it is aligned and attracts the best talent Coordinate the executive level engagement between regions, customers and senior stakeholders Leverage synergies across various sites and participates/leads in sharing best practices Coach and mentor supply chain professionals across the organization Create and promote a culture of collaboration, team-work and fun while delivering to or exceeding expectations Who we are looking for: Minimum Education and Experience Bachelor's Engineering Degree in risk management, industrial Safety and Health, Safety engineering, Safety management, or closely related field 10-15 years’ leadership experience in regional or global manufacturing environment Knowledge and expertise in safety requirements in international locations (Americas and Europe) Proven ability to lead diverse safety teams to achieve organizational objectives Experience in the interpretation and enactment of Safety standards in OSHA and other global regulations Demonstrated ability to establish, implement, and manage best practice environmental, health & safety programs Familiarity with ISO 9001/14001/18001 implementation and program sustainability Ability to lead in a matrix environment Highly developed interpersonal communication skills with the ability to effectively, persuasively, and tactfully interact with employees at all levels of the organization. Highly effective presentation and training delivery skills Demonstrated ability to quickly establish credibility and lead by influence across all levels of the organization, from senior leadership to individual contributors This is a remote, U.S.-based role with willingness and ability to travel internationally to manufacturing sites. Build an effective team committed to organizational goals; foster collaboration among team members. Solution oriented, proactive approach and attitude in resolving issues without compromising quality Strong leadership, mentoring, organizational and communication skills Required Skills and Education - 15+ Years Management/Supervision Experience - Leadership experience in global manufacturing operations required Preferred Skills and Education -Experience in global organization -Experience leading teams through impact/influence -Experience in large scale industrial manufacturing

title: Environment Health Safety Lead
description: About Us PEG is an international engineering and contracting company with a presence across selected strategic geographies. With over 50 years of proven experience , PEG delivers process design, engineering solutions, and project management services across the Oil & Gas, Power Generation, and Renewables sectors. Our capabilities cover the full project lifecycle, from conceptual and front-end engineering design (FEED) and feasibility studies through detailed engineering, construction, commissioning and start-up, to operations and maintenance . About the Role Location: Iraq/ Basra and other project Locations Position: HSE Lead Key Responsibilities: Developing and implementing comprehensive health, safety, and environmental policies in accordance with legal and corporate guidelines. Conducting risk assessments to identify potential hazards and developing preventative strategies. Organizing safety training for employees to ensure awareness and understanding of safety and environmental practices and legislation. Monitoring compliance with policies, performing site inspections, and preparing detailed reports on findings. Leading emergency response initiatives and conducting investigations after incidents to establish causes and preventive measures. Advising on a range of specialist areas, e.g., fire regulations, hazardous substances, noise, occupational diseases, and waste management. Maintaining current knowledge of legislation and regulatory requirements related to health, safety, and environmental matters that impact the organization. Collaborating with internal leadership and external regulatory bodies to maintain compliance standards. Implementing health and safety plans that comply with company policies and legislated standards. Overseeing environmental performance and adherence to legal environmental standards. Handling safety/regulatory audits both internally and externally. Coordinating with HR departments to ensure physical examinations and medical clearances are completed per the company's policies. Developing and maintaining documentation related to HSE initiatives, such as inspection forms and training modules. Qualifications and Experience: Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Science, Safety Management, or a related field. NEBOSH IGC certification Professional certifications such as Certified Safety Professional (CSP) or Certified Industrial Hygienist (CIH) are highly desirable. Strong understanding of the legal health and safety guidelines relevant to the industry. Several years of experience in a HSE role, ideally within the industry or a closely related field. Proficient use of HSE management software and tools. What We Offer: Opportunity to work on strategically important Oil & Gas projects. International and multicultural working environment. Competitive compensation package. Professional growth and leadership opportunities within a dynamic project organization.
